chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Noah (peace be upon him), when he was in the days of the flood, called upon all the waters, so they responded to him except for the water of sulfur and the bitter water, so he cursed them both.
ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Noah curse the sulfur and bitter waters during the flood?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) commands the waters of the flood, yet sulfur and bitter waters remain disobedient, leading him to curse them. This event is cited by Shia scholars to explain the distinct physical and spiritual properties of these waters, often linking their resistance to divine will with their classification as *khabith* (impure) or their unique utility in healing and preservation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When Noah<sup>as</sup> was during the days of the flood, called all the waters. So they all responded except for the sulphuric water, and the bitter water, so he<sup>as</sup> cursed them both’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Nuh, Alayhi al-Salam, in the days of flood called all waters and they all replied except water of the sulfur and bitter water which then he condemned.’”
